Artist on Instagram: "For decades, the true identity of the street artist Banksy has remained unknown. A Reuters report published on March 13, 2026 claims the artist may finally have been identified as Robin Gunningham, a 51-year-old man from Bristol. Banksy’s artworks have appeared on streets around the UK and around the world since the early 1990s, often carrying political and social messages while the artist stayed completely anonymous.

The report links Banksy to old police and court documents from a 2000 arrest in New York for allegedly defacing a billboard, where the name Robin Gunningham reportedly appears alongside a handwritten confession. Gunningham is also said to have changed his name to David Jones in 2008, possibly to avoid being identified.

Banksy’s authentication company, Pest Control, and his lawyer Mark Stephens declined to confirm or deny the claim, warning that revealing the artist’s identity could violate his privacy and interfere with his work.

#banksy #streetart #urbanart #graffitiart #contemporaryart"

The man doesn't wish to be identified, let him do great things in peace. Anonymity is the part of the charmHonestly, I think the journos who did this do not have ethical values. There is a reason he didn't want his identity known. This should not be seen as pride (on investigators) it should be seen as shame!It is incredibly sad.We really didn’t care to know the real identity. The mystery was more interesting and fun.We love his art and don't need to know who he is :)Biggest spoiler alert that nobody wanted.Banksy is Banksy and that’s enough. His work is relevant his name is not. It speaks for itself.Hot topic: The Epstein FilesReuters: let’s find out who Banksy really is🤦🏻‍♂️Not a fan of this. In a culture where anonymity is crucial to do the work. this feels like violation.Same feeling as finding out about SantaIt feels deeply unfair that after decades of powerful, thought-provoking street art, people are still trying to expose Banksy’s identity. The anonymity has always been part of the message... the art should matter more than the artist. Trying to unmask him doesn’t serve the culture of art; it only satisfies curiosity at the cost of an artist’s privacy. Let the work speak for itself.🎈We don’t want to know. Respect his privacy and let’s just appreciate the Art he shares with us.
